description:
Connection to a real Authentik server. Cluster-scoped — an org-wide,
shared piece of infrastructure, not owned by a single namespace.

secretStore.description:
Where this instance's oauth2 application credentials are written:
the backend of the implicit target of an `AuthentikApplication`
without `secretTargets` (default `kubernetes`), and the Vault
connection every Vault target uses.

caSecretRef.description:
Optional custom CA certificate to verify Vault's TLS with, read from
a Kubernetes `Secret` (the referenced `key` must hold a PEM bundle).
Use this to trust a private CA (e.g. openbao-tls) without mounting
it into the operator pod — the operator reads the Secret via the
API and hands the PEM to its Vault client. When unset, the system
trust store is used. Only consulted for `https://` Vault addresses.

kubernetesAuthMount.description:
Mount path of Vault's Kubernetes auth backend. Defaults to
`kubernetes`, Vault's own default mount name.

kubernetesAuthRole.description:
Vault Kubernetes-auth role this operator authenticates as — its
own ServiceAccount JWT is exchanged for a Vault token via
`auth/<kubernetesAuthMount>/login`. See `.prompt/plan.md`'s note
on `vault.tf`'s OIDC federation for why a Vault-aware `SecretStore`
exists at all (unrelated to this auth step, which is the
operator authenticating *to* Vault, not Vault federating
Authentik as an OIDC provider).

mount.description:
KV v2 secrets engine mount (e.g. `secret`) credentials are written
under.

pathGrants.description:
Paths outside `<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/` that the
`AuthentikApplication`s of the listed namespaces may write to (an
application publishing its credentials where its consumer already
reads them). A grant opens its paths to everyone allowed to create
an `AuthentikApplication` in a covered namespace; it never hands
over a value another CR owns. The Vault policy of
`kubernetesAuthRole` stays the hard bound: restrict it to the same
paths.

items.description:
Paths of the instance's secret backend that objects may write to
outside their namespace's subtree `<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/`. Opens
them to every subject allowed to create an emitting object in a
covered namespace, and cannot hand over a value another object owns.

clusterScoped.description:
The grant opens `paths` to cluster-scoped objects (instead of
`namespaces`).

namespaces.description:
Namespaces whose objects may write `paths`: exact names, `*`, or a
prefix glob such as `team-*`. `team-*` opens the paths to every
matching namespace.

paths.description:
Path patterns under the mount, compared segment by segment: a
literal segment matches itself, `+` exactly one segment, and a last
`*` one or more. Each holds at least one literal segment, e.g.
`shared/auth`, `+/auth`, `platform/*`. Prefer exact paths where
values not written by the operator live: a covered object may take
over a value no object owns yet.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a path pattern has no "." or ".." segment
a path pattern has at least one literal segment
a grant names namespaces or is clusterScoped, not both

pathPrefix.description:
Path prefix under `mount` — a target's default KV path is
`<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/<name>` (`<namespace>/<name>` when empty),
and an `AuthentikApplication` may only write under
`<pathPrefix>/<its namespace>/`, unless `pathGrants` opens a path to
it.

An empty prefix makes every namespace's subtree a top-level folder
of the mount: a namespace named like a folder that holds other
values (one a grant opens, `shared/` say) owns that folder — its
objects write there without any grant. Keep a prefix unless the
mount is reserved to per-namespace folders and no namespace can be
created with the name of another top-level folder.

tls.description:
TLS verification for the API connection above — a private CA to trust
(`tls.caSecretRef`), or the `tls.insecureSkipVerify` escape hatch.
Defaults to plain platform-trust-store verification.

caSecretRef.description:
Optional custom CA certificate to verify the instance's TLS with,
read from a Kubernetes `Secret` (the referenced `key` must hold a PEM
bundle). Use this to trust a private CA without mounting it into the
operator pod — the operator reads the Secret via the API and hands the
PEM to its HTTP client. It is added *on top of* the platform trust
store, so publicly-signed endpoints keep working. When unset, only the
platform trust store (plus the usual `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`
env vars) is used.

insecureSkipVerify.description:
Skip certificate verification entirely — insecure, intended only for
throwaway/self-signed instances. Prefer `caSecretRef` below, which
trusts a private CA without turning verification off.

tokenSecretRef.description:
A key inside a Kubernetes `Secret` in an explicit namespace — used by
cluster-scoped CRDs, which have no namespace of their own to default to.

url.description:
Base **web** URL of the Authentik instance, e.g.
`https://login.example.com` — not the `/api/v3` REST endpoint, which
is derived from it (see [`split_urls`]). This is the root the
per-application OIDC issuers hang off,
`<url>/application/o/<slug>/`, so it is what oauth2 consumers end up
trusting.
